thread:
emily (PM): we just got word that the 3rd-party SSO vendor delayed their v2 API. this will impact the SSO pilot we planned for v1. immediate ask: do we freeze timeline and pull SSO into v2, or eat the integration work now and push other items? short answers pls.

jon (eng-lead): initial read: SSO v2 delay blocks our end-to-end customer pilot but only affects a subset of tenants. we can cut SSO from v1 if we accept a lighter pilot for tenants without enterprise SSO. cutting it frees ~3 sprint-weeks.

amir (sre): SSO integration also required DB schema changes and a migration window. that plus cert rotation means higher ops risk during launch. pulling it reduces release risk.

belle (design): product experience note: removing SSO forces a fallback signup path for pilot users. we need to ensure flows are clear and we don't add onboarding friction. design effort ~1 sprint.

tana (product-ops): landing constraints: execs want at least 2 strategic customers in pilot. both currently require SSO. if we cut SSO, we lose those two. that changes customer acceptance criteria.

chris (data): metric impact: without those strategic tenants our early activation metric target drops by ~12pp in simulations. that matters for go/no-go signals.

emily (PM): ok trade space: Option A) postpone launch 2 weeks and keep current pilot with SSO once vendor is available. Option B) cut SSO to v2, run smaller pilot, keep launch date. Option C) keep date and build a temporary proxy integration to simulate SSO (hacky, ops heavy).

jon (eng-lead): engineering preference: B + mitigation. build a lightweight feature flag toggle so we can re-enable SSO quickly when vendor is live. that avoids rework and keeps code paths isolated.

amir (sre): ops mitigation: if we cut SSO, add a "pilot-only" deploy window and smoke-tests for signup/backfill. also require DB migration dry-run in staging before launch.

belle (design): for B we produce a minimal fallback onboarding flow and a short copy doc explaining enterprise limitations. estimate: design + microcopy = 4 dev-days.

tana (product-ops): process decision: we need to update the milestone tracker, acceptance criteria, and notify the two customers immediately with options. I'll draft the comms.

chris (data): propose we set conditional acceptance: launch proceeds if post-cut pilot activation >= baseline - 8pp. if below, we triage to schedule a fast follow.

emily (PM): i'm leaning B (cut SSO) to avoid a full timeline reset. but we must be explicit about the conditions that would force a reset: 1) vendor indefinite delay (>4 weeks) 2) customer churn risk materializing 3) critical regulatory blocker.

roadmap-bot: milestone-tracker updated: planned-launch: 2024-05-10, current-status: feature-cut applied, SSO moved to v2.

jon (eng-lead): action items: 1) eng to add feature-flag + revert plan (owner: jon, ETA: 5 dev-days). 2) infra to schedule DB migration dry-run (owner: amir, ETA: 3 days). 3) design to ship fallback flow (owner: belle, ETA: 4 days). 4) PM to update milestone tracker and customer comms (owner: emily/tana, ETA: today).

amir (sre): will also add a runbook entry for signup backfill in case we need to migrate enterprise users later.

belle (design): will attach quick screenshots to the milestone tracker so execs can review without waiting for a demo.

tana (product-ops): i'll schedule a 20m cut review today and put the updated acceptance criteria in the tracker.

emily (PM): final note: please annotate your card with the "timeline-risk" tag (low/med/high) and a one-line justification. we'll use that to decide fast resets if something else pops up.

jon (eng-lead): tagged SSO card as high risk with justification: external vendor dependency + DB migration.

chris (data): i'll run the post-cut activation sim and post results within 24h.

emily (PM): thanks everyone. consensus: proceed with Option B (cut SSO to v2), keep launch date, apply mitigations above. we'll revisit if vendor reports >4wk delay or if activation sims miss the conditional acceptance threshold. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
